subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs / deployment topology

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs / deployment topology

Alex / Sanjay — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared context.

Key pain points you shared:
- User-facing document summarization is adding 300–600ms of extra latency per request today due to in-house batching logic and model fan-out.
- Peak concurrent queries hit ~350 qps during business hours; tail latency spikes during bursts are causing user-visible errors.
- Data residency and audit log requirements: logs retained for 12 months, and no customer PII leaves your VPC unless explicitly allowed.

Goals from the call:
- Bring p95 end-to-end latency under 250ms for 1–2k token requests for interactive summarization.
- Maintain sustained 400–500 qps with graceful degradation and 99.9% availability for peak windows.
- Ensure any Private/Dedicated deployment meets FinApps security controls (KMS integration, audit trails).

Technical notes / hypotheses:
- Recommended model: a quantized 7B variant for the summarization endpoint (good balance of latency and quality); fallback to a higher-capacity 13B planned for batch/overnight jobs.
- Serving topology: Dedicated pool for interactive traffic (GPU-backed, autoscale with burst headroom) + Private control plane for audit/KMS. Edge routing by region to keep cross-region latency minimal.
- Latency levers: continuous batching with per-customer KV caching, request-level timeout policies, and optimized kernel selection for your sequence lengths.

Attachments I’m sharing: SLO_memo.pdf (short SLO targets & test harness), redwood-network-diagram.png (proposed VPC peering & proxy layout).

Open questions we promised to follow up on:
1) Can you share your current request size distribution (tokens per request) and exact 95/99 latency numbers for the interactive flow?
2) Any compliance blockers for running Dedicated / Private with our control plane?
3) Do you have a preferred RTO/RPO for incident recovery beyond the 99.9% availability target?

Proposed next steps:
- Dev + Rishi to draft an SLO feasibility note and a proposed Dedicated sizing plan (I’ll circulate by EOD tomorrow).
- Follow-up technical session with your infra team to validate VPC/network constraints (target next week).
- Pilot contract & SOC2 evidence exchange once we align on topology.

Thanks — Marissa

Alex — thanks for the numbers; that histogram will be very helpful. A few technical calls-outs from our runtime side: 

- For your token distribution (median 220, 99th 1.8k) we recommend splitting interactive requests into two classes: short (<600 tokens) handled by a low-latency 7B quantized model with aggressive KV caching, and long (>600 tokens) routed to a separate pool with higher memory (13B) to avoid tail amplification on the interactive pool. That reduces p95 for short requests significantly while preserving quality for long ones.
- To hit p95 < 250ms for short requests at 400 qps, we’ll size a dedicated pool with continuous batching and a target batch latency budget of 15ms for kernel execution. We’ll include a burst reserve of ~25% to absorb sudden spikes.
- Network topology: recommend VPC peering between FinApps and our Dedicated cluster plus a Transit Gateway in region for multi-AZ failover. Keep the control plane access via a private endpoint; we can support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) and TLS mutual auth for audit streams.
- Observability: we’ll instrument token-level latency, batch sizes, kernel selection, and cache hit rates. We’ll also provide a synthetic harness to reproduce tail spikes.

I’ll attach a quick sizing table and an example nginx/proxy layout in the follow-up note.

Cheers,
